result.summary: Scope test: real executable surface (export/2, import/3) -- full procedure, not skipped. Wrote test/specs/REQ-034.md (4 ACs, each with rationale beyond restating the criterion) and test/letflow/definitions/export_import_test.exs (5 tests, real Postgres via Letflow.DataCase, async: false, per-test provisioned tenants, unique_name/1 + Ecto.UUID.generate() identifiers, no shared fixtures). AC1: 1 test, chains source-row graph == export/2's document.graph == import/3's returned imported.graph == the imported row re-read directly from Postgres, using a graph with a nested attributes map plus an unrelated extra key to catch shallow-copy bugs. AC2: 2 tests -- baseline (different-tenant import gets a fresh id) plus the literal edge case: a real pre-existing row is inserted directly (via a pre-set non-nil :id on the struct, since create/2's changeset never casts :id) under document.id in the target tenant before import, then import/3 is proven to assign a distinct id and leave the pre-existing collision row unmodified (count_by_id unchanged, name/version unchanged). AC3: 1 test -- import/3 vs. a direct Definitions.create/2 call built from the exact attrs import/3's own design (doc doc Sec4.3 step I1) constructs, asserting the two returned {:error, {:graph_validation_failed, violations}} values are identical (not just both-error), proving no separate/diverging validation path. AC4: 1 test -- an otherwise-fully-valid document (valid graph/name/version) with bpm_export_schema_version != 'bpm/definition/v1' is rejected with the exact {:error, {:unknown_schema_version, actual}} tuple, with an explicit refute against the graph_validation_failed shape it would need if the gate were bypassed. Per REVIEWER's Step 2d non-blocking note, :tenant_id_not_accepted and :initial_status_not_draft (create_error() variants structurally unreachable through import/3's own attrs builder) are deliberately not covered. Verified: MIX_ENV=test mix do compile --warnings-as-errors + test --warnings-as-errors test/letflow/definitions/export_import_test.exs -> 5 tests, 0 failures, 0 warnings. Full test/letflow/definitions/ directory (271 tests) also passes with 0 failures -- no regression. One pre-existing, unrelated warning (valid_review_attrs/1 in promotion_review_migration_test.exs, confirmed present with export_import_test.exs removed) blocks --warnings-as-errors only at the whole-directory level, not attributable to this change. mix format --check-formatted clean on both new files.
